name: CardCheck — API on RapidAPI
description:
Catch mistyped card numbers before they fail at the gateway: CardCheck validates card numbers locally (Luhn checksum plus issuer rules) and identifies the card network — one at a time, or in batches of up to 100 — with a definitive verdict and the individual checks shown.

What you get:
- A valid / invalid verdict per number, computed locally — no card data leaves the validation logic
- The individual checks behind the verdict (length, Luhn checksum, IIN/BIN range), so your UI can explain what is wrong
- Card network identification (e.g. Visa, Mastercard, Amex) for form formatting, icon display and routing decisions
- Batch results in the same per-number format, ready to feed screening and import pipelines
- A networks reference endpoint listing the supported networks and their number patterns

Key endpoints:
- GET /validate — validate one card number and identify its network
- POST /validate/batch — validate up to 100 card numbers in one call
- GET /networks — supported card networks and their patterns

Batch / built for workflows:
CardCheck sits at the front of checkout and signup flows as a pre-validation gate — one fast local-computation call per number before anything reaches your payment gateway — and the batch endpoint extends the same checks to list screening, onboarding imports and data-quality jobs: up to 100 numbers per call, one structured result per number. It validates number structure only: it does not check funds, card status or fraud risk, and it is not a substitute for your payment processor's checks.

Access: subscribe on RapidAPI (free tier available); calls are made over HTTPS with your RapidAPI key.
